questions.q: What is missing: 'Hi Neha, having a party at my place, do come! Love, Riya.'
questions.a: When and What-occasion — 'party' with no date, time, or reason is unusable. A wrong answer 'nothing' shows the logistics checklist isn't running.

questions.q: Reply to a birthday invite you can't attend — which line is right: 'Can't come, busy.' or 'So sorry Riya — we're visiting Nani that weekend. Hope it's the best party ever!'?
questions.a: The second — clear decline + reason + warmth. The first is curt to the point of rudeness; informal register still has manners.

questions.q: Does an informal invitation letter need the receiver's address block at top?
questions.a: No — informal letters carry only the sender's address + date. A wrong answer adding the receiver block merges the formal and informal skeletons.

questions.q: An informal invitation or reply inside a letter follows the ______ rules but adds event logistics: the invite must carry What/When/Where clearly, and the reply must accept or decline with a reason — both in first-person friendly register.

Fill in the blank: An informal ______ or reply inside a letter follows the warm-skeleton rules but adds event logistics: the invite must carry What/When/Where clearly, and the reply must accept or decline with a reason — both in first-person friendly register.
Fill in the blank: The ______ checklist inside the warmth: What (birthday dinner), When (Saturday 7 pm), Where (our place).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes an invitation containing all event logistics and a reply that accepts/declines with a stated reason, keeping informal register throughout.
